after.owned_result_provenance: 40 shared relationship cases and12 actual scheduling cases included in final277-case combined run.

behavior: Only direct final caller assertions set denied/affirmed; unknown remains unknown. Shared assertion filter retains default call-control behavior and opts into conservative direct-prefix checks for relationship facts.
Quoted, reported, conditional, negated and third-party assertions cannot overwrite the caller position. Merchant business type and customer-support occupation are not company relationships.
A genuine newer caller assertion supersedes an older one; ordinary questions never erase relationship evidence.

Explicit provider turn order prevents old assertion replay. A delayed first final can supply a newer relationship assertion than the last known relationship without replaying old action/contact/refusal fields.

Traditional first use bootstraps only earlier available caller history. A corrected current transcript reapplies only its relationship contribution against the bounded pre-current-turn snapshot, preserving later tool/contact/action state.
Typed UNKNOWN is authoritative; the guard never reimports a retracted assertion from the contact buffer. Legacy history API uses the same shared parser.

Depth-one response coalescing retains onlythe latest explicit relationship assertion from overwritten accepted queue entries, never dropped contact/action/refusal/stage state or fulltranscript. Current neutral replacement restores the predecessor; queue duplicates and false-barge replay preserve identity.
limitations: State lives for the existing call lifecycle; this does not add database persistence or transparent restart recovery.
No provider, PSTN, TTS or customer calls occurred. Native event ownership and submitted-speech integration have separate owner artifacts.
Deterministic relationship assertion coverage is conservative; these tests do not establish open-ended language comprehension or prevent every model invention.

Traditional compatibility callers without handler-owned accepted-dispatch metadata still use session counter/history length for current-turn identity only; they cannot prove cross-task temporal order. Raw media sequence is never used as that proof.

lint.result: passed on final source and test files

ordering_followup.contract: Use handler-owned task._caller_turn_order, allocated synchronously at accepted final or queue insertion; raw _utterance_seq is media-only. Exact duplicates retain accepted order, queue drain copies order, false-barge replay preserves it and rejects newer accepted turns. Stale owned tasks cannot replace current observation identity/digest. Latest explicit relationship from overwritten queue entries is retained as one immutable enum/order/id record; onlythree relationship fields are applied before current replacement baseline.

scheduling_before.note: Initial five tests before dispatch-stamp implementation; sixth real cancellation/replay control added afterward.

coalescing_before.symptom: Accepted queued denial overwritten by ordinary queue entry was lost before reduction.

warnings: Final run retained existing datetime.utcnow deprecations and one AsyncMock capture-mode warning in test_voice_pipeline_service; no application/provider/network operations occurred.
